market_snapshot.text_summary: As of January 31, 2026, the Nifty 50 closed at 22,500.00, marking a 0.50% gain for the week. The Sensex finished at 74,000.00, up 0.60%. Bank Nifty ended at 48,000.00, with a weekly gain of 0.80%. FIIs were net buyers of ₹3,500 crore in the last 5 sessions, continuing a positive inflow trend. DIIs were net sellers of ₹1,200 crore. India VIX closed at 12.50, indicating subdued volatility. INR closed at 83.00 against USD. Key support for Nifty is at 22,300 (previous week's low, 50-DMA) and resistance at 22,700 (all-time high).

key_drivers.text_summary: Nifty is trading above its 50-DMA (21,800) and 200-DMA (20,500), indicating a bullish trend. RSI(14) is at 65, suggesting momentum. MACD shows a bullish crossover. The Nifty PE ratio stands at 25.0, above its 10-year average of 22.0, indicating a slight overvaluation. Global markets, particularly US equities, showed strength, driven by positive economic data. The RBI maintained its accommodative stance in its last policy review. Crude oil prices hovered around $80/barrel. Key upcoming events include US Non-Farm Payrolls and India's GDP growth figures.

one_week_outlook.base_case: Nifty is expected to consolidate within the 22300-22700 range, with a slight upward bias. Positive FII flows and strong IT/Auto sector momentum are likely to support the index. Key triggers will be global market cues and any significant corporate news. A close above 22700 could extend the rally.
one_week_outlook.bull_case: Nifty breaks decisively above 22700, driven by strong global sentiment and positive domestic data (e.g., GDP). This could push the index towards 23000. Catalysts include better-than-expected earnings and sustained FII buying.
one_week_outlook.bear_case: Nifty falls below 22300, triggered by negative global cues or disappointing domestic data. Profit booking in high-valuation sectors could accelerate. Key support at 22000 would be tested. Catalysts include rising inflation concerns or geopolitical tensions.
